assessment: The microtubule motor cytoplasmic dynein-1 transports diverse membrane-bound organelles, but in most cases the mechanism of cargo recognition is unknown. Christensen, Kendrick, and colleagues use BioID, in vitro assays, and live-cell fluorescence imaging to show that the three Hook family cargo adaptors form complexes of distinct composition with proteins of the FHIP family. They map how specific FHIP proteins recruit dynein to different endosome and Golgi compartments. This study provides evidence for a new mechanism through which activation of dynein motility is coupled to the selection of cargo.
